ideas.title: Venezuela homecoming, Iran next
ideas.hook_en: Venezuela just watched its opposition leader come home. Iranians are counting down to the day Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi can return to Iran too. Javid Shah.
ideas.visual: Side-by-side image: the Machado return photo (credit source) next to a Reza Pahlavi portrait, caption 'Next: Iran'.
ideas.angle: Ride the Venezuela news cycle that Iranian accounts are already quote-posting.
ideas.why: Seen in outsider posts from @DearPenFriend (758 likes) and @Mehrdad_rst in the last 48h.

ideas.title: What 'Javid Shah' actually means
ideas.hook_en: Why do Iranians chant Javid Shah? It is a cry for freedom and a national referendum, not a call for absolute rule. Here are the points people keep misunderstanding.
ideas.visual: 5-slide carousel, one point per slide, Persian + English text, Lion and Sun flag on the last slide.
ideas.angle: Counter the 'monarchy = absolutism' narrative with the referendum point already circulating.
ideas.why: A similar explainer thread by @NSn43386568 is active in the last 48h; a clean carousel version is easier to share.

ideas.title: Pezeshkian: 'cowards' and begging
ideas.hook_en: In one breath the Islamic Republic's president calls Americans cowards. In the next he begs for a deal. This regime has no one who can speak for Iran - Iranians already chose their voice.
ideas.visual: 30s screen-recorded video of the state TV clip with English captions and a closing card 'Iranians choose Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi'.
ideas.angle: Use the regime's own words to show its contradictions, then pivot to the alternative.
ideas.why: The @siaxares posts on Pezeshkian and Trump drew 4.8K and 4.4K views, the best English regime-news posts of the sample.

ideas.title: Hand the embassies to the people
ideas.hook_en: Governments keep talking to the Islamic Republic's diplomats. Iranians are asking them to expel the regime's envoys and recognize Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi as the voice of the people.
ideas.visual: Map graphic of countries already tagged in campaigns (Australia, Argentina, New Zealand, Belgium) with a flag pin each.
ideas.angle: Turn scattered appeal posts into one shareable campaign visual.
ideas.why: At least 4 country variants of this appeal are circulating in the sample.

ideas.title: Then vs now: Tehran before and after 1979
ideas.hook_en: Before 1979 and after. Watch what the Islamic Republic did to Iran, and what a free Iran can look like again.
ideas.visual: 20-30s split-screen archive clips, 3 caption beats, credits in the last frame.
ideas.angle: Copy the then-vs-now format of the 263K-view Yemen post, applied to Iran.
ideas.why: @realMaalouf's then/now Yemen clip hit 263.6K views; format transfers to the Iran/Pahlavi niche.

ideas.title: Frankfurt, November 7
ideas.hook_en: Frankfurt, November 7: Iranians in Europe are calling for people to turn out. Be the voice of those who cannot speak.
ideas.visual: Poster-style image with date, city, Lion and Sun, and a QR link to the official event page (verify the source before posting).
ideas.angle: Event-promo posts are circulating; verify the organizer before amplifying.
ideas.why: Two Frankfurt Nov 7 posts appear in the 48h sample.

why_hit.note: Broad Muslims-vs-non-Muslims claim; huge reach comes from outrage and quote-fights, not Iran niche.
Short street-interview clip with a punchline; sarcasm on the last line drives replies.
Then-vs-now footage plus a collapse thesis: simple contrast format that travels fast.
Clip of a woman speaking plus an ethnic-slavery claim; heavy quote/outrage engagement.
Two-word hook on breaking news; curiosity gap, no content in the text.
Persian-language rhetorical question about an unpopular journalist; likes-to-views is high. 7-day fallback hit (Oct 21), not inside the 48h window.
Hijab-related confrontation line with a quoted clip; high likes-to-views (14.6K likes on 85K views).
Election-doubt question after a Brazil result; reply-bait (479 replies).
Outrage story with a clip about a child-abuse case; moral shock.
Conspiracy-style claim about European riots; heavy bookmarking/sharing.
Video reaction of a bereaved father (Persian) to a public figure's comments on the 18 Dey protesters; emotional + video + the account's 196K audience.
Two-word Persian caption on a media post; the video does the work and the caption is a verdict.
